operations.specification: Create a registration endpoint for the member actor based on the civic_board_users table. This operation inserts a new record into civic_board_users using fields email, password_hash (derived from submitted password), display_name, and initializes email_verified to false and suspended to false. It should also create an initial session in civic_board_user_sessions (fields: civic_board_user_id, ip, href, referrer, created_at) and may issue an email verification token by inserting into civic_board_email_verifications (actor_type="user", email, token, expires_at, used=false) plus a specialization row in civic_board_email_verification_of_users linking the token to the new user via civic_board_user_id. Successful registration returns JWTs in an authorized payload while persisting an audit trail via civic_board_audit_logs as appropriate. Prisma tables directly involved: civic_board_users (primary), civic_board_user_sessions, civic_board_email_verifications, civic_board_email_verification_of_users, and optionally civic_board_audit_logs for audit entries.
operations.description:
This operation registers a new member account by creating a record in civic_board_users. It consumes the submitted email to populate civic_board_users.email, stores a cryptographic password hash in civic_board_users.password_hash, and saves the user-facing name in civic_board_users.display_name. New accounts are created with civic_board_users.email_verified set to false and civic_board_users.suspended set to false. Timestamps civic_board_users.created_at and civic_board_users.updated_at are set to the current UTC time.

Upon successful creation, the system records a session entry in civic_board_user_sessions tied with civic_board_user_sessions.civic_board_user_id to the new user. Connection context from the request is captured in civic_board_user_sessions.ip, civic_board_user_sessions.href, and civic_board_user_sessions.referrer with civic_board_user_sessions.created_at set to the current UTC time. The session remains active until civic_board_user_sessions.expired_at is populated by a later logout or session revocation.

If email confirmation is required, an email verification token is produced by inserting a row into civic_board_email_verifications with actor_type set to "user", email mirrored into civic_board_email_verifications.email, a unique civic_board_email_verifications.token, and civic_board_email_verifications.expires_at scheduled according to policy while civic_board_email_verifications.used remains false. The token is linked to the user by creating a specialization row in civic_board_email_verification_of_users referencing civic_board_email_verification_of_users.civic_board_email_verification_id and civic_board_email_verification_of_users.civic_board_user_id.

Security logic enforces uniqueness on civic_board_users.email (per the @@unique constraint) and applies initial eligibility rules using civic_board_users.email_verified and civic_board_users.suspended. Passwords are never persisted in plain text; only civic_board_users.password_hash is stored.

Related operations include POST /auth/user/login for subsequent authentications, POST /auth/user/email/verify/request for re-sending verification tokens, and POST /auth/user/email/verify/confirm for token confirmation. Failures such as duplicate email or invalid input yield clear validation errors while preserving safe behavior.

On success, this endpoint issues an authorized response containing access credentials appropriate for subsequent requests and may optionally record an audit entry in civic_board_audit_logs using fields like actor_type, action, outcome, and created_at to provide compliance visibility.
operations.summary: Register a new member in civic_board_users and return authorized tokens.

requestBody.description: Registration payload containing email, password, and display name.

responseBody.description: Authorized session and token package for the newly registered user.

operations.name: join

operations.specification: Create a login endpoint for member users backed by civic_board_users and civic_board_user_sessions. The operation validates submitted credentials against civic_board_users.email and civic_board_users.password_hash. On success it creates a session row in civic_board_user_sessions (civic_board_user_id, ip, href, referrer, created_at) and returns JWTs. It should deny login when civic_board_users.suspended is true or civic_board_users.deleted_at is not null (treated as non-active account). Rate limiting metadata can be enforced using civic_board_rate_limits with scope values such as "login.failed" to track failed attempts. Audit entries may be recorded in civic_board_audit_logs.
operations.description:
This operation authenticates a member by comparing the supplied email with civic_board_users.email and verifying the password against civic_board_users.password_hash. When the match succeeds and civic_board_users.suspended is false, a session record is written to civic_board_user_sessions with civic_board_user_sessions.civic_board_user_id pointing to the authenticated user and context values captured in civic_board_user_sessions.ip, civic_board_user_sessions.href, and civic_board_user_sessions.referrer. Session start is recorded in civic_board_user_sessions.created_at and remains in effect until civic_board_user_sessions.expired_at is set by a logout or revocation.

Login attempts are subject to anti-abuse controls. Failed attempts can increment counters in civic_board_rate_limits by scope (e.g., scope="login.failed") using actor_type such as "user" and the current user identifier in civic_board_rate_limits.actor_id. The window is defined by civic_board_rate_limits.window_started_at and civic_board_rate_limits.window_ends_at, with civic_board_rate_limits.count and civic_board_rate_limits.limit guiding enforcement.

Email status in civic_board_users.email_verified can be surfaced to guide post-login capabilities. Accounts marked suspended via civic_board_users.suspended (and optionally civic_board_users.suspended_at) are denied authentication to prevent further access until an admin action clears the restriction.

On successful authentication, the server returns an authorized payload. The application may also create an entry in civic_board_audit_logs noting actor_type ("user"), an action such as "auth.login", the outcome, and timestamps for traceability without coupling to foreign keys.

Related flows include POST /auth/user/refresh for renewing tokens, POST /auth/user/logout for ending the current session, and POST /auth/user/logout/others for terminating other sessions associated with this user.
operations.summary: Authenticate a member via civic_board_users and create civic_board_user_sessions, returning authorized tokens.

requestBody.description: Credentials for member authentication by email and password.

responseBody.description: Authorized session and token package for the authenticated user.

operations.name: login

operations.specification: Provide a token refresh endpoint that renews short-lived access using a submitted refresh artifact while validating the session against civic_board_user_sessions. The server checks that the referenced session is active (civic_board_user_sessions.expired_at is null) and associated to a valid user in civic_board_users (e.g., not suspended). On success, issue new tokens and optionally rotate refresh artifacts. Audit with civic_board_audit_logs when appropriate.
operations.description:
This operation accepts a refresh request and validates that the underlying session remains valid. The application associates the provided refresh artifact with a row in civic_board_user_sessions and ensures civic_board_user_sessions.expired_at is not set. It also confirms that the linked user in civic_board_users exists, is not suspended per civic_board_users.suspended, and remains eligible for continued access (email status in civic_board_users.email_verified can inform feature gates).

If validation passes, new access credentials are returned, optionally rotating the refresh artifact and updating the session context as needed. Session creation time is preserved in civic_board_user_sessions.created_at; expiration is still governed by civic_board_user_sessions.expired_at when logout or revocation occurs.

Security considerations include rejecting refresh when the session is not found, when civic_board_user_sessions.expired_at is present, or when civic_board_users.suspended is true. Implementations may record an event in civic_board_audit_logs capturing actor_type, action (e.g., "auth.refresh"), and outcome.

Clients typically call this endpoint after receiving an access token expiry. It complements POST /auth/user/login and POST /auth/user/join, which initially create the authenticated context.

Failures return descriptive errors without disclosing sensitive details such as password or token internals.
operations.summary: Refresh access credentials by validating civic_board_user_sessions for a member user.

requestBody.description: Refresh request containing the refresh artifact associated to an active session.

responseBody.description: Authorized session and token package with renewed access credentials.

operations.name: refresh

operations.specification: Issue or re-send an email verification token for the authenticated user by inserting a new row into civic_board_email_verifications with actor_type="user", email, token, expires_at, used=false and linking it via civic_board_email_verification_of_users to civic_board_users.id. This operation requires an authenticated member (authorizationActor "user").
operations.description:
This operation helps a signed-in member obtain a fresh email verification token. It creates a token in civic_board_email_verifications with actor_type set to "user", copies the current account email into civic_board_email_verifications.email, stores a newly generated civic_board_email_verifications.token, sets civic_board_email_verifications.expires_at in UTC, and leaves civic_board_email_verifications.used as false with civic_board_email_verifications.used_at null until confirmation.

The token is strictly associated to the member by creating a companion row in civic_board_email_verification_of_users that references civic_board_email_verification_of_users.civic_board_email_verification_id and civic_board_email_verification_of_users.civic_board_user_id. These links ensure unambiguous ownership and later confirmation can set civic_board_users.email_verified to true.

Because this is a user-initiated action, it requires an authenticated context and uses the current principal’s civic_board_users.id. No email address needs to be passed if the server reads it from civic_board_users.email, but the request may include optional metadata used for delivery.

On success, the server may enqueue delivery and returns an acknowledgement payload. Errors include attempting to request tokens for accounts that do not exist or sending when the member is already verified according to civic_board_users.email_verified.

This endpoint is commonly used with POST /auth/user/email/verify/confirm, which consumes the token and flips the civic_board_users.email_verified flag upon success.
operations.summary: Create an email verification token in civic_board_email_verifications linked to the current civic_board_users row.

requestBody.description: Optional parameters for sending email verification (e.g., delivery hints).

responseBody.description: Summary acknowledgement of verification token issuance.

operations.name: requestEmailVerification

operations.specification: Confirm a user’s email using a submitted token by validating a row in civic_board_email_verifications (actor_type="user", token matches, within expires_at, used=false), updating civic_board_email_verifications.used and civic_board_email_verifications.used_at, and setting civic_board_users.email_verified=true via the relationship defined by civic_board_email_verification_of_users. This operation is public because it is usually triggered from a link.
operations.description:
This operation consumes a previously issued verification token to confirm email ownership. It looks up a record in civic_board_email_verifications by civic_board_email_verifications.token, ensuring actor_type equals "user", civic_board_email_verifications.expires_at is in the future, and civic_board_email_verifications.used is false. On success, it marks civic_board_email_verifications.used as true and sets civic_board_email_verifications.used_at to the current UTC time.

To update the account, it follows the specialization link from civic_board_email_verification_of_users, reading civic_board_email_verification_of_users.civic_board_email_verification_id and civic_board_email_verification_of_users.civic_board_user_id to identify the target user row in civic_board_users and sets civic_board_users.email_verified to true. The account’s civic_board_users.updated_at is updated to reflect the change.

Security considerations include preventing replay after civic_board_email_verifications.used is set, validating the token lifetime using civic_board_email_verifications.expires_at, and ensuring the token’s actor_type matches a member account. The operation avoids exposing whether specific emails exist by using generic error messages when validation fails.

This confirmation endpoint is typically reached from an emailed link and does not require an authenticated session. It aligns with the issuance endpoint POST /auth/user/email/verify/request which generates the token.

Upon success, a simple acknowledgement is returned, and the system may log an event to civic_board_audit_logs for compliance visibility without coupling through foreign keys.
operations.summary: Confirm email by consuming civic_board_email_verifications and updating civic_board_users.email_verified.

requestBody.description: Verification token payload for email confirmation.

responseBody.description: Summary acknowledgement of successful email verification.

operations.name: confirmEmailVerification

prerequisites.description: A verification token must have been issued for the user before the confirmation can consume it. The issuance creates the civic_board_email_verifications row (actor_type="user") linked via civic_board_email_verification_of_users, which the confirm operation requires to validate and mark as used.

operations.specification: Accept a password reset request for a member by creating a row in civic_board_password_reset_tokens with actor_type="user", token, expires_at, used=false and linking it via civic_board_password_reset_token_of_users to civic_board_users.id found by the submitted email. Public operation without authentication.
operations.description:
This operation initiates a password reset for a member account by emitting a token that permits a one-time password change. It inserts a record into civic_board_password_reset_tokens with actor_type set to "user", generates a unique civic_board_password_reset_tokens.token, sets civic_board_password_reset_tokens.expires_at to a policy-driven time in the future, and initializes civic_board_password_reset_tokens.used as false with civic_board_password_reset_tokens.used_at left null until consumption.

To associate the token with the correct user, a specialization row is created in civic_board_password_reset_token_of_users linking civic_board_password_reset_token_of_users.civic_board_password_reset_token_id to the token and civic_board_password_reset_token_of_users.civic_board_user_id to the identified civic_board_users row corresponding to the submitted email. The parent civic_board_users record is not modified at this stage.

Security behavior avoids leaking account existence by returning a uniform acknowledgement regardless of whether a matching civic_board_users.email was found. Rate limiting can be enforced using civic_board_rate_limits by scope such as "password.reset.request" with actor_type set appropriately.

This request endpoint pairs with POST /auth/user/password/reset/confirm which validates the token and sets a new password. Tokens are one-time and time-limited as defined by civic_board_password_reset_tokens.expires_at and civic_board_password_reset_tokens.used.
operations.summary: Create a password reset token in civic_board_password_reset_tokens for a member identified by email.

requestBody.description: Email submission for password reset initiation.

responseBody.description: Summary acknowledgement that a reset flow has been initiated.

operations.name: requestPasswordReset

operations.specification: Confirm a password reset by validating a token in civic_board_password_reset_tokens (actor_type="user", token matches, within expires_at, used=false) and then updating civic_board_users.password_hash for the linked account derived via civic_board_password_reset_token_of_users. Marks the token as used by setting civic_board_password_reset_tokens.used=true and civic_board_password_reset_tokens.used_at to current time.
operations.description:
This operation consumes a password reset token to set a new credential for a member account. It reads civic_board_password_reset_tokens by civic_board_password_reset_tokens.token, checking actor_type equals "user", that civic_board_password_reset_tokens.expires_at is still in the future, and that civic_board_password_reset_tokens.used is false. On success, it resolves the target user through civic_board_password_reset_token_of_users using the pair civic_board_password_reset_token_of_users.civic_board_password_reset_token_id and civic_board_password_reset_token_of_users.civic_board_user_id.

The user’s credential is updated by computing a new hash and writing it to civic_board_users.password_hash while updating civic_board_users.updated_at. After the change, previously active sessions may be ended by setting civic_board_user_sessions.expired_at for that user’s other sessions as a security measure.

The reset token is marked consumed by setting civic_board_password_reset_tokens.used to true and civic_board_password_reset_tokens.used_at to the current UTC time to prevent reuse.

This operation is public and does not require the member to be signed in. It is intended to follow POST /auth/user/password/reset/request which created the token.

A success acknowledgement is returned. Implementations may also append an audit entry into civic_board_audit_logs with an action such as "auth.password_reset.confirm" and the outcome for traceability.
operations.summary: Consume civic_board_password_reset_tokens to set a new civic_board_users.password_hash for the associated user.

requestBody.description: Token and new password for password reset confirmation.

responseBody.description: Summary acknowledgement of successful password reset.

operations.name: confirmPasswordReset

prerequisites.description: A password reset token must be issued before it can be confirmed; the issuance operation creates the valid token that the confirmation consumes.

operations.specification: Allow an authenticated member to change their password by verifying the current credential and updating civic_board_users.password_hash. After a successful change, end other active sessions by setting civic_board_user_sessions.expired_at for sessions belonging to the user except the current one. Enforce security using civic_board_users.suspended when necessary.
operations.description:
This operation changes the password for the signed-in member. It first validates the submitted current credential against civic_board_users.password_hash. When the check succeeds and the account is eligible (civic_board_users.suspended is false), it computes a new hash and writes it to civic_board_users.password_hash, updating civic_board_users.updated_at.

To protect the account, the server should revoke other concurrent sessions by populating civic_board_user_sessions.expired_at for all sessions linked via civic_board_user_sessions.civic_board_user_id except the current session. The current session remains valid so the user can continue operating after the password change.

This endpoint requires an authenticated context and uses the caller’s civic_board_users.id; no explicit user identifier is passed in the path. Business logic may enforce password complexity policies while ensuring the database persists only the hash in civic_board_users.password_hash.

Typical errors include incorrect current password, attempts by accounts marked as suspended via civic_board_users.suspended, and constraint violations in password policies. On success, the response returns a concise outcome description.

Use this endpoint in conjunction with POST /auth/user/logout/others when you need to proactively terminate other sessions even without changing the password.
operations.summary: Update civic_board_users.password_hash for the current member and revoke other sessions.

requestBody.description: Current and new password for an in-session password change.

responseBody.description: Summary of password change and session revocation outcome.

operations.name: updatePassword

operations.specification: Invalidate the current authenticated member session by setting civic_board_user_sessions.expired_at for the caller’s active session. The user’s identity is the source of truth; no path parameter is needed. Returns a session summary acknowledgement.
operations.description:
This operation ends the caller’s current session. The server identifies the active row in civic_board_user_sessions for the authenticated context and sets civic_board_user_sessions.expired_at to the current UTC time, leaving an immutable record of session start in civic_board_user_sessions.created_at. No other user properties are modified.

This action is restricted to authenticated members and uses the current session derived from the authorization context. It does not alter civic_board_users.email_verified or civic_board_users.suspended; it strictly ends the session.

Security considerations include idempotent behavior: calling logout when civic_board_user_sessions.expired_at is already set simply acknowledges completion without error.

This endpoint complements POST /auth/user/login and POST /auth/user/refresh by terminating the session when no longer needed. For revoking other sessions, use POST /auth/user/logout/others.

A concise acknowledgement payload is returned on success.
operations.summary: End the current session by updating civic_board_user_sessions.expired_at for the caller.

responseBody.description: Session termination acknowledgement summary.

operations.name: logout

operations.specification: Invalidate all other active sessions for the authenticated member by setting civic_board_user_sessions.expired_at for sessions whose civic_board_user_id matches the caller and session id differs from the current one. Used after sensitive changes such as password updates.
operations.description:
This operation revokes all sessions belonging to the authenticated member except the one used to call this endpoint. The server locates rows in civic_board_user_sessions via civic_board_user_sessions.civic_board_user_id and sets civic_board_user_sessions.expired_at for each session that is currently active and not the present session.

This is a security-focused operation intended to clean up stale or potentially compromised sessions. It leaves the current session intact and does not modify civic_board_users fields such as email, display_name, or suspended. Audit logging may record the action for traceability.

The endpoint requires an authenticated context and relies on the caller identity from authorization to scope the revocation to the correct account. No path parameters are necessary.

Use this endpoint after password changes or other sensitive updates to ensure that tokens derived from other sessions can no longer be used.

A brief acknowledgement is returned indicating completion of the revocation.
operations.summary: Revoke other sessions by updating civic_board_user_sessions.expired_at for all of the caller’s other sessions.

responseBody.description: Summary acknowledgement of other-session revocation.

operations.name: logoutOthers

operations.specification:
Create a new administrator account and establish the initial authenticated context. This operation writes a new row to the civic_board_admins table (columns: email, password_hash, display_name, email_verified=false, suspended=false, created_at, updated_at) and, upon success, records an authenticated session in civic_board_admin_sessions (columns: civic_board_admin_id, ip, href, referrer, created_at). It may also enqueue an email verification flow by issuing a token in civic_board_email_verifications (actor_type="admin", email, token, expires_at, used=false) and linking via civic_board_email_verification_of_admins (civic_board_email_verification_id, civic_board_admin_id).

The endpoint responds with JWT-based authorization payloads for the admin actor (access/refresh tokens) and the admin’s profile summary required for subsequent privileged operations. This operation is the canonical entry point for administrator registration and is tied to the admin actor lifecycle maintained by civic_board_admins.
operations.description:
This endpoint registers a new administrator using the civic_board_admins table. The table stores the credential hash in password_hash, the unique email in email, the public-facing display_name, and two control flags email_verified and suspended that govern posting/moderation eligibility. Creation and update moments are tracked in created_at and updated_at, while deleted_at exists for retention governance but is not used during registration.

On successful creation, an authenticated context is established by inserting into civic_board_admin_sessions. This relation requires civic_board_admin_id and captures ip, href, and referrer together with created_at. Session records can later be marked ended via expired_at by security flows such as logout or password changes.

For verification, the system may issue a token in civic_board_email_verifications with actor_type="admin", email, token, expires_at, and used=false. The token is linked specifically to the new admin through civic_board_email_verification_of_admins, which enforces a 1:1 mapping to the main token and requires civic_board_admin_id. These verification structures enable later confirmation that flips email_verified to true on the admin record.

Security considerations include enforcing @@unique([email]) on civic_board_admins to prevent duplicate accounts and checking the suspended flag to avoid creating active sessions for prohibited identities. Audit trails for the registration event can be recorded in civic_board_audit_logs using actor_type and action fields without introducing FKs.

Related operations are /auth/admin/login for credential authentication, /auth/admin/email/verification to request verification tokens, and /auth/admin/email/verify to consume a token. Password recovery is available through /auth/admin/password/reset/request and /auth/admin/password/reset using the password reset token tables designed for admin actors.
operations.summary: Register a new administrator in civic_board_admins and return admin authorization.

requestBody.description: Admin registration payload including email, password, and display name.

responseBody.description: Authorized admin after successful join with issued JWT tokens.

operations.name: join

operations.specification:
Authenticate an existing administrator by verifying credentials stored in civic_board_admins (email and password_hash) and create a new session record in civic_board_admin_sessions capturing connection context (ip, href, referrer, created_at). The response returns JWT authorization for the admin actor.

This operation reads civic_board_admins fields including suspended and email_verified to determine eligibility and may deny session establishment when suspended=true. Session lifecycle can later be updated by setting expired_at in civic_board_admin_sessions through logout or security flows.
operations.description:
The login flow validates the administrator’s email against civic_board_admins.email (unique) and verifies the provided password against password_hash. The account’s flags email_verified and suspended are consulted to determine whether authentication can proceed and whether privileged actions are allowed after login. Timestamps created_at and updated_at on the admin record provide audit-friendly context; deleted_at exists for retention policies and does not affect login directly.

Upon successful authentication, an entry is created in civic_board_admin_sessions linked by civic_board_admin_id. The session captures ip, href, referrer, and created_at for auditing and security analytics. Future security flows may set expired_at to end the session.

This operation issues JWT tokens for the administrator. The access token identifies the actor for protected routes, while the refresh token supports token renewal in a subsequent refresh operation. Neither token storage is modeled in the schema; instead, sessions in civic_board_admin_sessions provide the server-side audit trail.

Rate limiting and abuse prevention can leverage civic_board_rate_limits by tracking a scope such as "login.failed" per actor_type="admin"; while not mandatory for the operation, the table offers a structured store for counters and window timings (window_started_at, window_ends_at, count, limit).

Related operations include /auth/admin/refresh for token renewal, /auth/admin/logout to end the current session, and /auth/admin/password/reset/request for recovery when the password is forgotten.
operations.summary: Authenticate an administrator from civic_board_admins and return authorization.

requestBody.description: Admin login credentials (email and password).

responseBody.description: Authorized admin with issued JWT tokens after successful login.

operations.name: login

operations.specification: Renew administrator JWT tokens using a valid refresh token. This operation does not modify database rows directly but is associated with the civic_board_admin_sessions table as the server-side audit context for the admin’s authenticated activity. It responds with a fresh authorization payload for the admin actor.
operations.description:
Token refresh exchanges a valid refresh token for new authorization material for the admin actor. While refresh tokens are not persisted in the schema, civic_board_admin_sessions provides the session ledger (id, civic_board_admin_id, ip, href, referrer, created_at, expired_at) used in security analytics and audit.

During refresh, business logic may verify that the associated admin record in civic_board_admins remains eligible for authenticated activity, checking suspended status and, where relevant, email_verified. The admin record includes created_at, updated_at, and a retention-oriented deleted_at field that is not part of the refresh decision path.

The operation ensures continuity of access without re-sending credentials. If signals indicate that the session should be terminated (e.g., password changed), the implementation should refuse refresh and require re-authentication, optionally consulting civic_board_audit_logs for additional context.

No path parameters are required. The request contains the refresh token in a structured body; the response returns new access/refresh tokens alongside the authorized admin summary.

Related operations include /auth/admin/login to establish a new session and /auth/admin/logout to end an existing session. Password changes via /auth/admin/password can also revoke refresh eligibility by ending historical sessions using expired_at on civic_board_admin_sessions.
operations.summary: Refresh administrator authorization using a valid refresh token; ties to civic_board_admin_sessions for context.

requestBody.description: Refresh token exchange payload.

responseBody.description: Authorized admin with renewed JWT tokens after successful refresh.

operations.name: refresh

operations.specification: Issue an email verification token for the currently authenticated admin. Creates a row in civic_board_email_verifications (actor_type="admin", email, token, expires_at, used=false) and links it via civic_board_email_verification_of_admins (civic_board_email_verification_id, civic_board_admin_id). The admin’s email_verified flag in civic_board_admins is not changed by this request; it is updated by the verification confirmation endpoint.
operations.description:
This operation prepares the email confirmation workflow for an administrator. It inserts a token into civic_board_email_verifications using actor_type="admin" and the admin’s email. The token lifecycle is described by fields token, expires_at, used, used_at, and timestamps created_at/updated_at. A retention-oriented deleted_at field exists for policy control.

To bind the token to the admin identity, a 1:1 specialization row is written to civic_board_email_verification_of_admins with civic_board_email_verification_id and civic_board_admin_id. This table enforces uniqueness on the main token reference and records created_at for auditability.

The admin identity itself resides in civic_board_admins, which holds email, password_hash, display_name, email_verified, and suspended, together with created_at and updated_at timestamps. The request does not modify civic_board_admins; email_verified remains unchanged until confirmation.

Security considerations include limiting repeated requests using civic_board_rate_limits (e.g., a scope such as "email_verification.request"). Additionally, audit trails may be recorded in civic_board_audit_logs with action names like "admin.email_verification.request" without introducing foreign keys.

Related operation: /auth/admin/email/verify consumes the token and flips email_verified to true on the admin record when valid.
operations.summary: Create an email verification token for an admin using civic_board_email_verifications and link via civic_board_email_verification_of_admins.

requestBody.description: Request to issue an email verification token for the authenticated admin.

responseBody.description: Summary of the issued email verification request.

operations.specification: Confirm administrator email ownership by consuming a token issued in civic_board_email_verifications and linked via civic_board_email_verification_of_admins. The Prisma schema documents that attachments “inherit visibility rules from their parent civic_board_posts” and that each attachment stores a storage URI (uri), original_filename, content_type, and byte_size, with optional image_width and image_height for images. Only posts (not comments) can have attachments, and an uploader and session may be recorded for auditability.

Security and permissions: This operation requires an authenticated user actor. Provider logic must ensure the uploader owns the target post or otherwise has permission, and that the parent post’s state allows new attachments according to product rules. The uploader identity (civic_board_user_id) is derived from the authenticated context rather than from the request body. The parent post is specified by the path parameter and mapped to civic_board_post_id.

Validation and business rules: Enforce allowed types (e.g., image/jpeg, image/png, image/gif, application/pdf) and per-file size limits, and cap the number of attachments per post based on configured policy. Reject only the offending files when limits are exceeded in a multi-file flow; for this single-record endpoint, validate the single payload. Also enforce the uniqueness constraint on (civic_board_post_id, original_filename) to prevent duplicate filenames on the same post. If the parent post is not in a state that accepts new attachments, deny creation with a clear reason.

Related operations and behavior: Clients typically call this after creating a post or during a post-edit window, and may subsequently call GET /posts/{postId}/attachments/{attachmentId} to confirm persisted metadata. Errors include permission denied, limit violations, or not-available when the parent does not exist or cannot accept attachments.

operations.specification:
Update a specific post attachment record stored in the civic_board_post_attachments table, identified by its UUID and scoped under its parent post civic_board_posts. This operation enables controlled modification of attachment metadata and/or file pointer (uri) while enforcing business policies for allowed content types, size limits, per-post attachment count, and uniqueness of original_filename per post (@@unique([civic_board_post_id, original_filename])). The path parameters carry the postId (civic_board_posts.id) and the attachmentId (civic_board_post_attachments.id). The provider must validate that the target attachment actually belongs to the indicated post (civic_board_post_attachments.civic_board_post_id = postId) before applying an update. Ownership and time-window rules derive from the post’s lifecycle and the attachment’s uploader fields (civic_board_post_attachments.civic_board_user_id and optional civic_board_user_session_id).

The request body follows ICivicBoardPostAttachment.IUpdate and may include fields such as uri, original_filename, and content_type, as well as any other mutable columns defined in the DTO that map to real columns (e.g., byte_size and image dimensions when the underlying file is replaced). The response returns the fully updated ICivicBoardPostAttachment object. Implementers must ensure changes remain consistent with the civic_board_posts state (status: "Published" | "Hidden" | "Deleted") and business edit windows and must not violate the composite uniqueness on (civic_board_post_id, original_filename).
operations.description:
Modify an existing post attachment while adhering to the schema-level intent documented on civic_board_post_attachments and civic_board_posts. The civic_board_post_attachments table stores immutable file metadata and storage URI with columns such as uri (VarChar up to 80000), original_filename, content_type, byte_size, optional image_width/height, timestamps, and an optional deleted_at used for retention. Its relation to civic_board_posts is a required FK (post) that must be respected; an attachment always belongs to exactly one post. Before applying any update, the service verifies that the path’s {postId} corresponds to the row’s civic_board_post_id and that the path’s {attachmentId} matches the target attachment’s id.

Security and authorization are enforced using actor context from civic_board_users and, when present, civic_board_user_sessions captured on upload. As per business rules, authors may modify attachments of their own posts only within the allowed edit window for posts (civic_board_posts has published_at, edited_at, and status fields). Admins may act at any time per moderation policy. If an attachment has a non-null deleted_at, treat it as removed from active visibility and disallow ordinary updates.

This operation is tightly coupled to the underlying database entities. It updates columns on civic_board_post_attachments that are meant to change when a file pointer or metadata legitimately changes (e.g., uri, original_filename, content_type, byte_size, image_width, image_height) and refreshes updated_at. The unique constraint @@unique([civic_board_post_id, original_filename]) is enforced to prevent duplicate display names per post. Ensure any change remains coherent with the parent post’s status in civic_board_posts (status: "Published" | "Hidden" | "Deleted").

Validation rules include: honoring allowed MIME types (e.g., image/jpeg, image/png, image/gif, application/pdf), respecting size limits reflected by byte_size, and ensuring that attachment visibility follows the parent post’s visibility state. Related APIs commonly used together include: deleting an attachment (DELETE /posts/{postId}/attachments/{attachmentId}) and post editing endpoints that govern the author’s edit window. On errors, return business-appropriate outcomes for ownership violations, edit-window expiry, hidden/deleted parent states, uniqueness conflicts on original_filename, and attempts to update an attachment that does not belong to the given post.

Remove a specific post attachment row from civic_board_post_attachments identified by {attachmentId} and scoped by its parent post {postId}. The table includes a deleted_at column; therefore, this operation performs a soft deletion by setting deleted_at instead of physically removing the row, supporting retention and purge policies aligned with the business lifecycle. The path parameters are postId (civic_board_posts.id) and attachmentId (civic_board_post_attachments.id). The provider must verify that the attachment belongs to the specified post before proceeding.

This operation supports author-driven removal within the allowed post edit window and administrative moderation at any time. Attachment visibility always follows the parent civic_board_posts record (status: "Published" | "Hidden" | "Deleted"). When deleted, the attachment should immediately disappear from public listings and reads, while remaining retained for administrative purposes until purge jobs finalize permanent removal according to policy.

Permanently remove the attachment from active visibility by marking the civic_board_post_attachments record with a non-null deleted_at timestamp. According to the schema comments, attachments inherit visibility from the parent post and store immutable file metadata such as uri, original_filename, content_type, and byte_size. The presence of deleted_at indicates the record is no longer active. Before removal, confirm that the given {postId} matches the record’s civic_board_post_id and that {attachmentId} matches the target attachment’s id, preventing cross-post access.

Security and permissions follow the business rules: the author may remove attachments tied to their own post within the edit window described by civic_board_posts timestamps; admins may remove attachments at any time as part of moderation. Attempts to remove attachments on posts in states that disallow user actions (e.g., Hidden or Deleted for non-admins) must be denied. The operation writes only the deleted_at (and updated_at) columns in civic_board_post_attachments; it does not alter the parent civic_board_posts row beyond indirect visibility effects.

Error handling includes: not-available outcomes when the attachment is already deleted; ownership or session checks failing; parent-post mismatch between IDs; or business policy rejections (e.g., post state disallowing user actions). Related operations: updating an attachment (PUT /posts/{postId}/attachments/{attachmentId}) and post-level edit endpoints that determine whether the attachment may be modified by the author at this time.

This operation writes into the Moderation domain by creating one main report row in civic_board_reports and one specialization row in civic_board_report_of_posts that binds the report to the target post and the reporting user/session. The reporter identity (civic_board_user_id) and session (civic_board_user_session_id) are taken from the authenticated context, not from the client payload. Duplicate prevention is enforced by the composite uniqueness on civic_board_report_of_posts (civic_board_user_id, civic_board_post_id). The request body carries only the business fields the reporter provides (reason and optional note), while the path parameter provides the post identifier. Upon success, the created specialization record (ICivicBoardReportOfPost) is returned for immediate client display and follow-up navigation to admin review flows (resolved later by civic_board_moderation_actions).
operations.description:
Submit a moderation report for a post by providing a categorical reason and an optional note. The operation persists report metadata in civic_board_reports with fields reason (text), note (optional text up to the product’s business limit), status (string workflow state such as "pending" managed by application logic), and audit timestamps created_at and updated_at. The specialization civic_board_report_of_posts binds the report to the target post via civic_board_post_id and records the reporting user via civic_board_user_id and the originating session via civic_board_user_session_id. The specialization enforces a one-to-one link to the main report through civic_board_report_id.

Security and permissions: only authenticated users may file reports. The reporter is derived from the signed-in user and their current session; clients must not supply user identifiers directly. Rate limits and duplicate prevention apply per policy; duplicates are structurally prevented by civic_board_report_of_posts @@unique([civic_board_user_id, civic_board_post_id]) so the same user cannot report the same post twice.

Database relationships: the created main report row in civic_board_reports can later be resolved by administrators who record decisions (e.g., Hide, Delete, or No Action) in civic_board_moderation_actions with a 1:1 uniqueness on civic_board_report_id. The report’s status string in civic_board_reports is used by queue processing and can be updated as part of the moderation lifecycle.

Validation and behavior: the request must include a supported reason value and may include an optional note. The server validates that the referenced civic_board_posts.id exists and that the authenticated user has permission to report. If the target post is not visible to the reporter or no longer exists, the service responds with a not-available outcome. The table includes a deleted_at timestamp for retention policies; newly created reports will have this column null. Error handling includes duplicate report detection (based on the unique constraint), invalid reason values per business rules, and authorization failures for unauthenticated actors.

Related operations: administrators will use separate moderation endpoints to resolve reports by creating entries in civic_board_moderation_actions. Reporters may later query their own reports through list endpoints filtered by reporter identity (not part of this operation).

Use these relations when the UI needs to show target type or reporter context; however, core filtering in this operation focuses on fields physically present in civic_board_reports.

Access to this listing is restricted to administrators because reports may contain sensitive context and moderation notes. The operation is intended for back-office workflows such as triage, bulk review, and time-based monitoring. While reporters can query their own submissions via specialization-specific endpoints, the generic /reports list is reserved for admin use to prevent information disclosure.

From a data relationship standpoint, civic_board_reports has a 1:1 association with one specialization row and an optional 1:1 association to a civic_board_moderation_actions row recording the final decision (Hide, Delete, or No Action). Duplicate-report prevention is enforced at the specialization layer via composite unique constraints (for example, user + post or user + comment), and not on the civic_board_reports base table itself—providers should rely on those constraints when composing queries.

Validation and business logic include filtering by status (e.g., pending vs resolved), reason categories, and created_at ranges using the actual columns present in the table. Since civic_board_reports includes a deleted_at column, soft-deleted records are excluded by default unless an explicit include-deleted flag is provided by the request body; this matches retention and audit expectations.

This operation is designed to pair with GET /reports/{reportId} for detailed inspection and with moderation action creation endpoints (not defined here) that write to civic_board_moderation_actions. Errors to expect include authorization failures for non-admin actors and empty result sets when filters yield no matches. Pagination is stable and results are ordered by created_at desc by default, with optional sort overrides.

Security and permissions: Only administrators should access this endpoint because the action contains moderation decisions and administrative context. The civic_board_admins and civic_board_admin_sessions relations on the action record provide the administrative provenance for auditing. Non-admin actors should not be able to read these records directly.

Database relationship context: The civic_board_moderation_actions row is associated to a parent civic_board_reports entry via civic_board_report_id, and the civic_board_reports entry itself is specialized to either a post or a comment via civic_board_report_of_posts or civic_board_report_of_comments. Validation and expected behavior: If no moderation action exists for the specified reportId (because the report is still pending or has not been decided), the implementation should respond with a not-found outcome for this resource path. If an action exists, it returns the single action. The status field on civic_board_reports (e.g., "pending" or "resolved") is orthogonal but often correlates to the presence of an action.

This operation targets the civic_board_post_reactions table and uses the unique composite key (civic_board_user_id, civic_board_post_id) to ensure at most one active reaction per user/post pair. Given the path parameter postId (civic_board_posts.id) and the authenticated user context (civic_board_users.id), the service will either create a new reaction row or, if a historical row exists with deleted_at set, restore it by clearing deleted_at and updating timestamps. operations.description:
Create or re-activate a post reaction for the authenticated user. The underlying entity is civic_board_post_reactions, which records the reacting user (civic_board_user_id), the target post (civic_board_post_id), and lifecycle timestamps (created_at, updated_at, deleted_at). Per the schema comments, reactions provide toggle semantics by keeping history and marking the reaction inactive via the deleted_at timestamp rather than removing the row. When this endpoint is called, if no reaction exists for the (user, post) pair, a new row is inserted; if a prior row exists with deleted_at set, the reaction is re-activated by clearing deleted_at.

Security and authorization follow the actors domain: the reacting principal must be an authenticated user from civic_board_users. Application logic must enforce reaction policy from civic_board_reaction_policies, including that reactions are globally enabled (enabled=true), allowed on posts (allow_on_posts=true), and disallow self-like when allow_self_like=false. If max_reactions_per_user_per_day is present, rate limiting must be applied using civic_board_rate_limits as needed. The target post is validated using civic_board_posts.status to ensure reacting to Published content; Hidden or Deleted posts must reject new reactions for non-admin actors per requirements.

This operation relates to multiple Prisma entities. It writes to civic_board_post_reactions and reads civic_board_posts to validate status and ownership (for self-like prevention). It may also read civic_board_reaction_policies to check feature flags and quotas. The unique constraint on civic_board_post_reactions (civic_board_user_id, civic_board_post_id) guarantees a single active reaction per pair and supports idempotent behavior: calling create when an active reaction already exists simply returns the current record. Session linkage and audit can be recorded via civic_board_user_sessions and civic_board_audit_logs for traceability.

Validation and business rules include: the postId must reference an existing civic_board_posts.id; the actor must not be suspended (civic_board_users.suspended=false); reacting to one’s own post must be rejected when policies prohibit self-like; reacting to Hidden/Deleted posts must be rejected for non-admin users; daily per-user reaction quotas, if configured, must be enforced. Related operations include DELETE /posts/{postId}/reactions to deactivate the reaction for the same user/post pair.

Error handling expectations: not found or unavailable outcomes when the post is not visible; policy-disabled outcomes when reactions are turned off; ownership/policy violations for self-like attempts; quota/rate-limit outcomes when daily caps are exceeded; and idempotency where creating an already-active reaction returns the existing active state without duplication.

The table columns include: id (UUID PK), code (unique business identifier), enabled, allow_on_posts, allow_on_comments, allow_self_like, max_reactions_per_user_per_day (nullable integer), created_at, updated_at. The creation flow must ensure the provided code is unique and initialize timestamps appropriately.
operations.description:
Create a new reaction policy configuration that governs reactions behavior across the platform. According to the civic_board_reaction_policies schema, each policy has a unique code along with boolean flags enabled, allow_on_posts, allow_on_comments, and allow_self_like, plus an optional max_reactions_per_user_per_day integer. This API persists a new row with those values and returns the saved entity.

Security and permissions: Only administrator actors are authorized to create policies because these settings affect global user experience and moderation posture. The underlying table is designed for administrative management, and application logic reads the active policy (by code) at runtime.

Database relationship and runtime usage: The civic_board_reaction_policies table is independent but referenced by reactions flows on posts and comments (civic_board_post_reactions and civic_board_comment_reactions) to determine whether reactions are enabled and which constraints apply. No counters are denormalized in this table; it strictly stores configuration flags and an optional limit value.

Validation and behavior: The code column must be globally unique per the Prisma schema (unique index on code). Typical business validation ensures the code uses an acceptable identifier format and that max_reactions_per_user_per_day, when provided, is a non-negative integer consistent with policy. On success, the API returns the created policy with its persisted timestamps.

This operation modifies fields such as enabled, allow_on_posts, allow_on_comments, allow_self_like, and max_reactions_per_user_per_day while preserving the policy code identifier. The table columns are: id (UUID PK), code (unique), enabled, allow_on_posts, allow_on_comments, allow_self_like, max_reactions_per_user_per_day (nullable integer), created_at, updated_at.
operations.description:
Update a stored reaction policy using its unique business identifier code. The civic_board_reaction_policies schema defines code as a unique key, making it an ideal path parameter for addressing the target policy. This operation adjusts configuration flags—enabled, allow_on_posts, allow_on_comments, allow_self_like—and may set or clear max_reactions_per_user_per_day.

Security and permissions: Only administrator actors can modify reaction policies. Because these values control feature availability and constraints across users and content, updates must be limited to trusted administrators.

Database linkage and runtime effects: Although this table stands alone, the values are read by application logic that governs creation of records in civic_board_post_reactions and civic_board_comment_reactions. Changing a policy here immediately influences whether new reactions are permitted and under what constraints; it does not rewrite historical reaction rows.

Validation, behavior, and errors: The reactionPolicyCode path parameter must match an existing row’s code (global scope). Implementers should enforce consistent semantics (e.g., non-negative integers for max_reactions_per_user_per_day when provided). If no policy exists for the supplied code, the operation should return a not-found outcome. On success, the updated entity is returned with refreshed audit timestamps.

The operation targets administrator-managed feature flags governing reactions (posts/comments, self-like rule, optional per-user caps). Selection uses the globally unique code column (@@unique([code])); the underlying primary key is UUID id. Deletion is implemented as a soft deletion by setting deleted_at to the current timestamp to preserve auditability and allow eventual purge per retention policies. Returns the affected policy record so clients can confirm the final state.
operations.description:
Remove a reaction policy from service by marking it deleted. The civic_board_reaction_policies model ("Administrative policy controlling whether reactions are enabled and under what constraints") contains fields: code (unique selector), enabled, allow_on_posts, allow_on_comments, allow_self_like, max_reactions_per_user_per_day, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at. This endpoint uses the unique code to locate the policy and sets deleted_at to indicate soft deletion while preserving the row for audit and operational safety.

Only administrators may execute this action. Provider logic should also emit an audit entry into civic_board_audit_logs describing the action (e.g., action: "reaction_policy.delete", target_table: "civic_board_reaction_policies", target_id: <policy id>), but audit logging is internal to the service and not exposed via this API.

The selection relies on civic_board_reaction_policies.code (global scope uniqueness via @@unique([code])). If the code does not exist or the row is already marked deleted (deleted_at IS NOT NULL), the service should respond with a not-available outcome to avoid leaking internal state. Because policy rows influence runtime behavior of reactions on posts and comments, removing a policy should be coordinated with configuration reads; clients are responsible for selecting an appropriate fallback policy after deletion.

Validation notes: reactionPolicyCode must be a non-empty string and match an existing, currently active policy (deleted_at IS NULL). Business logic should prevent deletion when the policy is the only active policy required by the platform’s configuration. Related operations typically include creating or updating reaction policies; reads should filter out rows with deleted_at set.

Error handling expectations: not found/not available for unknown codes; conflict if a guard prevents deletion (e.g., active/default policy); and generic failure handling consistent with service-wide exception rules. Records are not physically removed by this endpoint; they are soft-deleted and later purged by retention processes.

operations.specification: Provide an administrator dashboard overview aggregating moderation-related metrics across multiple tables. This read-only operation composes data from: civic_board_reports (queue of user-submitted reports and statuses), civic_board_moderation_actions (admin resolutions with decision values such as "No Action", "Hide", "Delete"), civic_board_posts (status: "Published" | "Hidden" | "Deleted"), and civic_board_comments (status: "Published" | "Hidden" | "Deleted"). It returns a computed DTO (ICivicBoardModerationOverview) summarizing pending counts, recent decision trends, and visibility distributions. No single Prisma table maps to the response; results are computed via SQL aggregations (e.g., COUNTs grouped by status/decision, date-bucketed trends).
operations.description:
This operation returns a consolidated moderation overview for administrators. It summarizes the current state of user-reported items from civic_board_reports ("User-submitted moderation requests ... status such as 'pending' or 'resolved'") alongside resolution records stored in civic_board_moderation_actions ("Captures the acting admin and session with the chosen decision 'No Action' | 'Hide' | 'Delete'"). Additionally, it includes visibility distributions of content from civic_board_posts (status with "Published", "Hidden", "Deleted" and timestamps such as published_at/edited_at) and civic_board_comments (status with the same values) to help admins understand the moderation footprint.

Security and permissions: Access is restricted to admins because the response may include sensitive moderation pipeline information and counts of hidden or deleted content. Provider logic should record an administrative read audit in civic_board_audit_logs for visibility into dashboard access while keeping the endpoint itself read-only.

Underlying entities and relationships: reports can be specialized to posts via civic_board_report_of_posts and to comments via civic_board_report_of_comments; each report can have at most one civic_board_moderation_action resolution. Aggregations typically include: number of pending reports, resolved reports by decision, recent (e.g., last 7 or 30 days) resolution counts, counts of posts and comments by status, and optionally per-day buckets derived from created_at or published_at for trend lines.

Validation and behavior: This endpoint does not accept filters in the minimal scope and always returns the current overview snapshot. If needed later, a PATCH variant could add time window or scope parameters. It never modifies any data. Related operations include report queue listing and resolution endpoints. Error handling should follow general rules: unauthorized for non-admin actors and system-busy/temporary errors where applicable.
operations.summary: Retrieve an aggregated moderation dashboard overview computed from reports, moderation actions, posts, and comments.

responseBody.description: Moderation overview metrics and trend snapshots for administrative dashboards.

operations.name: overview

operations.specification: Compute aggregated moderation statistics grouped by reason across all report records. This operation reads from the civic_board_reports table (primary source for report metadata) and produces a summary of total counts per reason. The specialization tables civic_board_report_of_posts and civic_board_report_of_comments are not directly grouped but guarantee target binding and duplicate prevention at creation time via their composite uniqueness constraints; counting is performed at the main civic_board_reports layer to avoid double-counting. Records with deleted_at set are excluded from aggregation to reflect active historical data. Example SQL (conceptual): SELECT reason, COUNT(*) AS count FROM civic_board_reports WHERE deleted_at IS NULL GROUP BY reason ORDER BY count DESC.
operations.summary: Summarize counts of civic_board_reports by reason for administrator insight.
operations.description:
Return a system-wide summary of moderation reports grouped by their categorical reason. The underlying data comes from the civic_board_reports model, which stores the reporter-selected reason, optional note, workflow status, and timestamps (created_at/updated_at). By summarizing at the main report layer, the service provides an at-a-glance view of where moderation attention is focused without exposing individual report details.

Access to this endpoint is restricted to administrators because it reveals platform-wide moderation patterns. The reports table is described as user-submitted moderation requests with a workflow state such as "pending" or "resolved." This endpoint respects logical removals by excluding rows where deleted_at is present so that the summary reflects currently retained report data per policy.

From a data relationship perspective, each civic_board_reports row must be bound to exactly one specialization row in either civic_board_report_of_posts or civic_board_report_of_comments. Those specialization models record reporter identity, target (post or comment), and session, and also enforce duplicate prevention via composite uniqueness (same user cannot report the same item twice). This aggregation intentionally groups only by civic_board_reports.reason and does not attempt to re-join to targets, ensuring consistent counting semantics.

Validation and behavior: the reasons are treated as free-form categorical values per schema comments (validated at the application layer during report creation). This endpoint groups whatever categorical values exist in the data. If no reports exist, the result contains an empty collection. Related administrative endpoints may include queues or detailed report listings, but those are distinct from this high-level summary.

responseBody.description: Aggregated counts by report reason for moderation analytics.

operations.name: index

operations.specification: Produce a daily time series of report volumes using civic_board_reports as the source. The operation groups by the UTC calendar day derived from created_at and counts how many reports were filed on each day. Specialization tables civic_board_report_of_posts and civic_board_report_of_comments are not required for aggregation but ensure that each report has a concrete target and that duplicates are prevented at creation time. Records with deleted_at set are excluded to align with retention behavior. Conceptual SQL: SELECT DATE_TRUNC('day', created_at) AS day, COUNT(*) AS count FROM civic_board_reports WHERE deleted_at IS NULL GROUP BY day ORDER BY day DESC.
operations.summary: Daily counts of civic_board_reports grouped by created_at day for admin trends.
operations.description:
Return a per-day time series of moderation reports to support trend analysis and operational planning. The data is sourced from the civic_board_reports model, which records each report’s reason, optional note, workflow status, and timestamps. Grouping is performed on created_at truncated to day in UTC, yielding the number of reports submitted each calendar day.

This endpoint is intended for administrative use only because it exposes system-wide moderation activity levels. Consistent with the schema’s lifecycle fields, rows where deleted_at is populated are excluded to reflect active retained data. The summary does not expose individual reporter identities or target references, honoring the principle of presenting aggregated information only.

Entity relationships: while every report is specialized via exactly one of civic_board_report_of_posts or civic_board_report_of_comments, this aggregation operates at the main civic_board_reports layer and does not join to the specializations. This avoids double-counting and keeps the computation efficient. Expected behavior: if no reports exist for a given day range, the time series will omit those days (sparse series). Clients may post-process to backfill missing dates if a continuous series is desired. Related operations include reason-based summaries and administrative queues that surface pending vs resolved counts.

responseBody.description: Daily time series of report volumes derived from civic_board_reports.created_at.

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves aggregated analytics for content reports by querying the Moderation domain tables centered on civic_board_reports and its specializations civic_board_report_of_posts and civic_board_report_of_comments. It supports time-window filtering (created_at), categorical slicing by reason and status, and breakdowns by target type (post vs comment). The provider composes SQL that groups and counts report records, optionally joining to Articles tables (civic_board_posts, civic_board_comments) to respect current visibility/status fields when required by filters. The endpoint is designed for administrative dashboards to monitor reporting trends and moderation workload. It does not create or modify any data; it summarizes existing rows.

The primary Prisma DB tables referenced are:
- civic_board_reports: carries reason, note, status, created_at/updated_at columns and is the anchor for analytics.
- civic_board_report_of_posts and civic_board_report_of_comments: identify the concrete target and reporter context and enforce duplicate-prevention via composite unique constraints.
- Optionally, civic_board_moderation_actions: used to slice metrics by resolved outcomes when joining on civic_board_report_id.

The request body accepts search/filter parameters modeled as ICivicBoardReport.IRequest (e.g., time range based on created_at, reason/status filters, and target-type selector). The response returns a computed analytics object ICivicBoardReportAnalytics containing counts and breakdowns suitable for dashboards (totals, by-reason, by-status, and time-bucket series).
operations.description:
Retrieve administrative analytics summarizing user-submitted content reports. The computation is anchored on the civic_board_reports table, whose columns include reason (categorical reason such as Spam/Harassment/Off-topic/Other), optional note, status (queue state like "pending" or "resolved"), and created_at/updated_at timestamps. The specialization tables civic_board_report_of_posts and civic_board_report_of_comments bind each report to its concrete target and reporter identity. Their composite uniqueness constraints (user+post or user+comment) allow detection of duplicates for analytics purposes without over-counting.

This endpoint is restricted to administrative actors because it exposes system-level operational insights. Use it to monitor volume over time, top reasons, resolution funnel, and distribution across posts versus comments. Implementations may optionally join to civic_board_moderation_actions to attribute decisions (e.g., "Hide", "Delete", "No Action") and to Articles tables (civic_board_posts, civic_board_comments) when filtering by current content status is necessary for policy reviews. The analytics query respects the provided filters and time windows and returns only aggregate structures; it never returns personal emails or raw free-text notes.

From a data-model perspective, analytics derive from:
- civic_board_reports: core event rows with reason, status, created_at.
- civic_board_report_of_posts / civic_board_report_of_comments: target-type discrimination, reporter and session context, and uniqueness guarantees to avoid double-counting.
- civic_board_moderation_actions: one-to-one resolution records per report, enabling breakdowns by decision.

Validation rules follow the underlying schema: reason and status filters must align with values stored in civic_board_reports; date filters apply to created_at ranges; and target-type accepts only post or comment determined by the specialization linkage. When no data matches, the endpoint returns zeroed totals with empty arrays. Authorization failures return an access-denied outcome, and malformed filters result in validation errors describing which field is incorrect.
operations.summary: Administrative analytics for reports based on civic_board_reports and related specialization tables.

requestBody.description: Filter, grouping, and pagination-like parameters for computing report analytics (time window on created_at, reason/status, target-type).

responseBody.description: Computed analytics object with totals, categorical breakdowns, and optional time-series for reports.

admin.description: Administrator who owns this session. Transformed association of civic_board_admin_sessions.civic_board_admin_id.

ip.description: IP address observed when the administrator session was established. Maps to civic_board_admin_sessions.ip.

href.description: Connection URL that initiated the admin session. Maps to civic_board_admin_sessions.href.

referrer.description: Referrer URL captured at session creation. May be an empty string for direct access. Maps to civic_board_admin_sessions.referrer.

created_at.description: Session creation time (UTC). Maps to civic_board_admin_sessions.created_at.

expired_at.description: Session expiration/end time (UTC), when applicable. Maps to civic_board_admin_sessions.expired_at.

ICivicBoardAdminSession.ISummary.description: Summary view of an administrator session from civic_board_admin_sessions for embedding as provenance in moderation action responses. Belongs-to admin reference is included as .ISummary to prevent circular expansion.

decision.description: Required decision to resolve the report. Allowed values reflect product policy (e.g., "No Action", "Hide", "Delete").

outcome_note.description: Optional moderator note explaining rationale. Persisted to civic_board_moderation_actions.outcome_note when provided.

ICivicBoardModerationAction.ICreate.description: Request DTO to create a moderation action for a specific report. page.description: 1-based page index for pagination. Applied at query time; does not map to a Prisma column.

limit.description: Maximum number of items per page (admin UIs typically use 20). Applied at query time; does not map to a Prisma column.

decision.description: Filter by moderation decision stored in civic_board_moderation_actions.decision. See Prisma comment: resolution outcomes include "No Action", "Hide", and "Delete".

report_id.description: Filter by the resolved report identifier (civic_board_moderation_actions.civic_board_report_id).

admin_id.description: Filter by the acting administrator identifier (civic_board_moderation_actions.civic_board_admin_id).

admin_session_id.description: Filter by the administrator session identifier (civic_board_moderation_actions.civic_board_admin_session_id).

include_deleted.description: Include soft-deleted records (where civic_board_moderation_actions.deleted_at IS NOT NULL) when true. Default is to exclude.

order_by.description: Sortable column for the list, typically created_at (default) or updated_at.

order.description: Sort direction to apply with order_by. Admin history views commonly use desc for newest-first.

ICivicBoardModerationAction.IRequest.description: Search, filter, sorting, and pagination parameters for listing moderation resolutions from Prisma table civic_board_moderation_actions. ICivicBoardPostReaction.ICreate.description: Request body for creating or re-activating a post reaction (civic_board_post_reactions). No fields are accepted: the target post comes from the path parameter, and the reacting user is taken from authentication context. Actor and path identifiers are intentionally excluded from the body.

id.description: Unique identifier of the post reaction record (UUID). Maps to civic_board_post_reactions.id.

user.description: Reacting user represented as a lightweight summary. Transforms civic_board_post_reactions.civic_board_user_id FK into an object for response readability.

post.description: Target post represented as a lightweight summary. Transforms civic_board_post_reactions.civic_board_post_id FK into an object to avoid N+1 lookups.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the reaction was first created (Like on). Maps to civic_board_post_reactions.created_at (UTC).

updated_at.description: Timestamp of last update including toggle operations. Maps to civic_board_post_reactions.updated_at (UTC).

deleted_at.description: Soft deletion timestamp used to represent Like off (inactive) while preserving history. NULL indicates the reaction is currently active. Maps to civic_board_post_reactions.deleted_at (UTC).

ICivicBoardPostReaction.description: Post reaction entity based on civic_board_post_reactions. Represents a single-like toggle per (user, post) pair using soft deletion semantics (deleted_at). Foreign keys civic_board_user_id and civic_board_post_id are exposed as summary objects to prevent N+1 calls and follow the BELONGS-TO → .ISummary transformation rule.

ICivicBoardCommentReaction.ICreate.description: Request body to toggle-on (create or restore) a single-like reaction on a comment. id.description: Primary key of the reaction row (UUID). Maps to civic_board_comment_reactions.id in Prisma.

user.description: Reacting actor transformed to an object reference (belongs-to). Derived from civic_board_comment_reactions.civic_board_user_id which references civic_board_users. Excluded raw FK per FK transformation rule.

comment.description: Target comment transformed to an object reference (belongs-to). Derived from civic_board_comment_reactions.civic_board_comment_id which references civic_board_comments. Excluded raw FK per FK transformation rule.

created_at.description: Creation timestamp (UTC) when the reaction was first added (Like on). Maps to civic_board_comment_reactions.created_at.

updated_at.description: Last update timestamp (UTC), including toggling operations. Maps to civic_board_comment_reactions.updated_at.

deleted_at.description: Soft deletion timestamp (UTC) representing Like-off toggle. NULL means the reaction is currently active. Maps to civic_board_comment_reactions.deleted_at.

ICivicBoardCommentReaction.description: Single-like reaction on a comment. Backed by civic_board_comment_reactions (Prisma). A row represents at most one (user, comment) pair via a composite uniqueness constraint and uses deleted_at for toggle semantics. Associations are transformed to objects for read DTOs: user (ICivicBoardUser.ISummary) and comment (ICivicBoardComment.ISummary).

civic_board_post_id.description: UUID of the target post whose reactions are being counted. Matches civic_board_posts.id. Included for clarity in read responses; source is the path parameter.

count.description: Number of active reactions (deleted_at IS NULL) for the target post, aggregated from civic_board_post_reactions.

ICivicBoardPostReactionCount.description: Aggregate view reporting the number of active reactions for a post. Computed by counting rows in civic_board_post_reactions where civic_board_post_id equals the requested identifier and deleted_at IS NULL. Providers should respect post visibility per civic_board_posts.status; if the post is not available to the caller, follow the service’s exception handling rules.
